requirement_catalog.statement: alpha_m and beta_n are supported on single dyadic intervals.
requirement_catalog.evidence: The outer prime ranges are explicit, but the switched remainders have not yet been partitioned into exact alpha/beta dyadic boxes.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Write each switched remainder before summation and freeze every dyadic box.

requirement_catalog.statement: Both sequences obey one fixed divisor-function order bound.
requirement_catalog.evidence: For a Cartesian G9 box, beta is bounded by 1 and alpha_m counts ordered prime pairs p2*p3=m, hence alpha_m<=tau_2(m). For G11/G12 the complementary alpha contains a p2-rough residual and its fixed-order bound has not yet been frozen.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Prove a uniform fixed-order divisor bound for the G11/G12 complementary rough-factor sequence.

requirement_catalog.statement: beta_n satisfies the exact residue-class asymptotic (3.2).
requirement_catalog.evidence: For fixed residue modulus h, Siegel-Walfisz on [Y,2Y] gives the required main term. Removing primes dividing d or N_global changes the two sides by O_h(tau_h(d)+1); h=1 is exact, and for h>=2 the number of relevant prime divisors is dominated by tau_h(d). Since Y is a fixed positive power of N_global, this is absorbed by Y*tau_h(d)/(log 2Y)^B for every fixed B.
requirement_catalog.next_action: State and prove the exact prime-sequence lemma matching (3.2), using distinct symbols for divisor order and residue modulus.
requirement_catalog.condition: beta_n is the characteristic function of primes in one frozen dyadic p1 block, with the fixed exclusion (n,N_global)=1
requirement_catalog.cannot_imply: This verifies the prime-beta sequence only; the exact switched decomposition must still prove that beta is p1 in every call.

requirement_catalog.condition: orientation O1 and sufficiently large p1 block
requirement_catalog.statement: beta_n vanishes when n has a prime factor below exp((log log n)^2).
requirement_catalog.evidence: A sufficiently large prime n has no prime factor smaller than itself.
requirement_catalog.cannot_imply: This conditional elementary check does not establish O1 or (3.2).

requirement_catalog.statement: M,N_beta and X=M*N_beta are fixed for the block.
requirement_catalog.evidence: For a G9 Cartesian product box, beta is supported in [P,2P], alpha in [M,2M], and the Lemma 3.5 scale is X=M*P. Boxes meeting epsilon*N_global<=mn<=N_global satisfy X>=epsilon*N_global/4.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Finish a disjoint or upper-cover Cartesianization of all cross-constraints and record boundary boxes.

requirement_catalog.statement: nu=log(N_beta)/log(X) is computed from the local scales.
requirement_catalog.evidence: In a G9 product box nu=log(P)/log(MP). Because MP is comparable to N_global with constants depending only on epsilon, nu equals the global p1 exponent up to O_epsilon(1/log N_global).
requirement_catalog.next_action: Trim the constant-width top p1 slice so every Lemma 3.5 box has nu<=1/10 exactly; send the trimmed slice to the classical estimate.

requirement_catalog.evidence: The lower global exponent 4/53 is safely above the lemma epsilon. The upper endpoint requires a constant-factor trim because X may be as small as epsilon*N_global/4.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Quantify the trimmed p1 slice and prove its contribution is O_epsilon(N_global/log^3 N_global) or absorb it with Lemma 3.1.

requirement_catalog.statement: lambda is order-1 well-factorable at the asserted level.
requirement_catalog.evidence: Lemma 2.5 produces a finite sum (l<=L) of order-1 well-factorable lambda_l^+ at level Q. Lemma 3.5 can be applied separately to each l; the fixed L=exp(8 epsilon^-3) must be carried into N0 and the global error ledger.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Bind the exact cell-dependent Q and confirm no convolution changes the order or level.

requirement_catalog.statement: The linear-sieve level equals X^(5(1-nu)/9-epsilon) up to an admissible loss.
requirement_catalog.evidence: For a frozen cell the intended level is Q=X^(5(1-nu)/9-epsilon). The displayed low-p1 coefficient has exactly this signature, but X, nu and logarithmic losses must be frozen cell by cell.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Write Q for every G9 cell and compare it with the level used in the switched linear sieve.

requirement_catalog.statement: The residue a lies in the stated uniform range |a|<=X.
requirement_catalog.evidence: Here a is the global even N_global, while X is a local dyadic product scale that may be smaller by an epsilon-dependent factor.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Prove |N_global|<=X under the normalization or justify a constant-multiple extension with tracked epsilon dependence.

requirement_catalog.statement: The lemma error is uniform over all boxes and parameters.
requirement_catalog.evidence: No blockwise constant ledger has been reconstructed.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Record dependencies on A, epsilon, order k and dyadic endpoints.

requirement_catalog.statement: All block errors sum within the global error budget.
requirement_catalog.evidence: Ordinary factor-2 dyadic decomposition produces only polylogarithmically many p1/p2/p3 cells, so arbitrary log-power saving can absorb the count. The boundary-cell main contribution still requires an explicit upper bound.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Prove the hyperbolic and ordering boundary cells contribute one extra logarithmic saving.

requirement_catalog.statement: The distribution level yields the displayed 36/5 and 8 coefficients.
requirement_catalog.evidence: For an upper bound, first use monotonicity S(B,P(N),N_global^(1/2))<=S(B,P(N),Q^(1/2)). Lemma 2.5 is then applied at z=Q^(1/2), so s=2 and F(2)=e^gamma. With V(z)~2*e^(-gamma)C/log z this gives 4/log Q, hence coefficient 4/theta(nu)=36/[5(1-nu)]; at nu=1/10 it is 8.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Derive the full normalization from Lemma 2.5 and the local Q.
requirement_catalog.condition: the local level Q and nu have been validly instantiated
requirement_catalog.cannot_imply: The exact coefficient bridge does not verify the sequence decomposition, level Q, or error uniformity.

candidate_orientation.beta_n: The smallest extracted prime p1 in one dyadic block.
candidate_orientation.alpha_m: For G9: the complementary product p2*p3, counted with multiplicity in a Cartesian box. For G11/G12: p2*p3*p4*r where r is the p2-rough residual counted by Buchstab, not necessarily a prime.
rationale: Only this orientation naturally makes the lemma's short variable nu track the displayed low-p1 exponent.
It explains why the paper changes theorem exactly at p1=N_global^(1/10).
It makes the beta sequence prime-supported, so the roughness condition is elementary and (3.2) has a plausible Siegel-Walfisz route.
It reproduces the displayed factor 36/[5(1-u)] if local nu=u.
The G9 switched multiset has product p1*(p2*p3); G11/G12 use Buchstab because the final residual is a rough integer rather than a prime.
cannot_imply: Structural preference is not a proof that the switched remainder has this exact convolution.
The local scale X and residue uniformity must still be checked.

calls.alpha_under_O1: Count of ordered prime pairs p2*p3=m in a frozen Cartesian box.
calls.call_specific_open_point: Cartesianize the p1-dependent inequalities so alpha is independent of beta, quantify boundary boxes, and justify the constant-multiple residue range.
calls.reduction: Up to O(N_global^(1-alpha)*log N_global+N_global^o(1)), G9 is bounded by prime quadruples N_global=b+p1*p2*p3 with p3>=p2, epsilon*N_global<=p1*p2*p3<=N_global and the stated p1,p2 ranges. The error covers residual factors p1 and prime divisors of N_global.

calls.alpha_under_O1: Count of factorizations m=p2*p3*p4*r in which r is the p2-rough residual estimated by Buchstab; r is not assumed prime.
calls.call_specific_open_point: Reconstruct the switched multiset and prove a fixed-order bound for the complementary rough-factor alpha sequence before importing the G9 template.

calls.alpha_under_O1: Count of factorizations m=p2*p3*p4*r in which r is the p2-rough residual estimated by Buchstab; r is not assumed prime.
calls.call_specific_open_point: Reconstruct the switched multiset and prove a fixed-order bound for the complementary rough-factor alpha sequence before importing the G9 template.

findings.statement: Lemma 3.5 has materially asymmetric assumptions on beta_n, so an unspecified alpha/beta orientation is not a cosmetic omission.
findings.cannot_imply: Does not show that no valid orientation exists.

findings.statement: Taking beta_n to be the smallest prime p1 is the structurally preferred orientation because it aligns the short-variable threshold with the paper's p1<N_global^(1/10) split.
findings.cannot_imply: The exact switched convolution and local scales remain unproved.

findings.statement: Under orientation O1, the small-prime-factor exclusion is automatic for sufficiently large p1 blocks; condition (3.2) has a plausible prime-in-progressions proof route but is not yet frozen.
findings.cannot_imply: Plausibility is not a completed uniform proof of (3.2).

findings.statement: For theta(nu)=5(1-nu)/9, one has 4/theta(nu)=36/[5(1-nu)], and the value at nu=1/10 is 8.
findings.cannot_imply: Matching the displayed coefficients does not verify the theorem call.

findings.statement: The application must reconcile the global residue a=N_global with Lemma 3.5's stated uniformity |a|<=X for each local dyadic product scale X.
findings.cannot_imply: This is a verification obligation, not a demonstrated counterexample or fatal gap.

findings.statement: The G11 and G12 derivation uses 'Similarly as before' and displays final integrals without recording the per-block Lemma 3.5 data.

For a frozen dyadic prime block beta_n=1_{n prime,(n,N_global)=1}, condition (3.2) follows from Siegel-Walfisz; the extra exclusions for divisors of d and N_global are absorbed by the tau_h(d) error factor.
findings.cannot_imply: This does not prove that every application actually has prime-supported beta.

findings.statement: The G9 sifted residual is a prime p3 outside squareful p1 and prime-divisor-of-N_global exceptions; these exceptions admit an O(N_global^(1-alpha) log N_global+N_global^o(1)) upper bound.
findings.cannot_imply: The subsequent switched multiset still needs a rigorous Cartesian dyadic decomposition.

findings.statement: The condition z<=Q^(1/2) in Lemma 2.5 is reconciled by upper-bound monotonicity: lower the sifting threshold to z=Q^(1/2). Then s=2 and the main coefficient is exactly 4/theta(nu), yielding 36/[5(1-nu)] and 8 at nu=1/10.
findings.cannot_imply: This does not validate Q or nu for a concrete block.

findings.statement: For G11 and G12 the complementary alpha sequence contains a Buchstab-counted rough residual; it should not be modeled as an additional prime without proof.
findings.cannot_imply: The corrected sequence has not yet been shown to satisfy a fixed-order divisor bound.

earliest_unresolved.stage: G9 Cartesian box compilation and residue-range bridge
earliest_unresolved.statement: The switched G9 multiset is identified and the prime-beta condition is proved, but the cross-constraints must be converted into alpha_m beta_n boxes and Lemma 3.5 must be justified for the constant-multiple range |N_global|<=C_epsilon X.

cannot_imply: This checkpoint does not pass or fail the complete G9, G11 or G12 applications.
The prime-beta lemma is conditional on the reconstructed orientation.
The constant-multiple residue extension of Lemma 3.5 remains unproved.
It does not independently verify Theorem 1.1 or binary Goldbach.

residual_analysis: Write N_global-b=p1*p2*r. If r is composite, its least prime factor is below p2 because p2>=N_global^(1/3).
A surviving least factor must divide N_global*p1. The factor p1 contributes a squareful error bounded by O(N_global^(1-alpha)*log N_global).
A prime factor of N_global forces the Goldbach prime b to equal that factor and contributes N_global^o(1) factorizations.
The case r=1 contradicts p1*p2>=epsilon*N_global for sufficiently large N_global because p1*p2<=N_global^(2/3).
g9_reconstruction.switched_multiset: B9 contains b=N_global-p1*p2*p3 with multiplicity, where p1,p2,p3 are prime and satisfy the G9 ordering and product constraints.
g9_reconstruction.prime_upper_bound: The original prime-b contribution is at most S(B9;P(N_global),N_global^(1/2))+O(N_global^(1/2+o(1))).
g9_reconstruction.dyadic_cell: For beta_n=1_{n=p1 in [P,2P]} and alpha_m=#{p2*p3=m in the cell}, the congruence is mn congruent to N_global modulo q and alpha_m<=tau_2(m).
g9_reconstruction.remaining_gap: The global inequalities are not Cartesian in p1 and m. A rigorous upper cover plus boundary estimate is still required.
